phases.label: Capital Clash · Saturday
phases.note: Capital and turrets leave protection 12:00–14:00 server time. Positioning opens 00:30. Hold-percentage decides the win, not total kills. All times are server time.

rows.label: Capital garrison
rows.detail: Strongest accounts, full-health formations, rotate every 45–60 min.

rows.label: Turret garrison (×4)
rows.detail: Each turret holds 10. Holding them bleeds the enemy capital 1% per tick.

rows.label: Rally lead
rows.detail: 3–5 rally accounts, full-capacity marches only. Rotate leads to beat fatigue.

rows.label: Reinforcement coordination
rows.detail: Refill marches to full before each send; recall half-capacity marches.

rows.label: Mud pressure / clear
rows.detail: Pressure enemy HQs and clear the brown dirt around the capital.

rows.label: Ruins clearing
rows.detail: Claim destroyed-HQ tiles quickly before the enemy teleports in.

rows.label: Point farm · HQ snipes
rows.detail: Knock out unshielded enemy HQs in the capital / Lv6 area — 50k points each.

rows.label: Reserve / on-call backup
rows.detail: Pinged to plug a gap or stand in for a core player whose phone dies.

phases.label: Prep phase · Sunday–Friday
phases.note: Prep points decide which state invades on Saturday. Everyone contributes daily — this is where the war is really won. All times are server time.

rows.label: Alliance Duel
rows.detail: 6,000 per member for 1st place + 30,000 alliance-wide per win.

rows.label: Furylord damage
rows.detail: Top-200 damage on the state scoreboard feeds state points.

rows.label: Arena
rows.detail: Champion is 20,000 state points. Max your heroes before reset.

rows.label: Truck raids
rows.detail: 100 points each and low risk — easy points that add up.

rows.label: Full Preparedness
rows.detail: Stack builds and training with the daily theme.

rows.label: Troop training (off-queue)
rows.detail: Keep training queues running and apply speedups so you are loaded for Saturday.

guide.headline: You are not here to bubble and watch.
guide.intro: Bubbling protects your base — it is not a job. Every member, at every HQ level, has real ways to score points and help us hold the capital. Pick your tier, pick a block on the board, and cover it.

tiers.title: Grass · HQ under 22
bullets: Reinforce the Capital and Turrets. You score from deployment time and from every kill your stationed troops make — and your own base never leaves its shield.
Garrison a turret slot. Each turret only holds 10 troops, so a full slot matters more than power. Turret kills are your points.
Farm safe points: truck raids (+100 each), Full Preparedness, and your daily Alliance Duel participation.
Join rallies when a lead calls one — joining scores without risking your base.
Be the reserve. When a core player drops offline you keep their slot warm. This is a real job and we will ping you for it.
Keep healing and retraining so you always have troops ready to send.

tiers.title: Mid · HQ 22–24
bullets: Mud pressure — clear the brown dirt around the capital and pressure enemy HQs.
Ruins clearing — when an HQ is destroyed, claim that tile before the enemy teleports in. This decides who owns the space.
Reinforcement coordination — refill every march to full capacity before it lands and recall half-capacity marches.
Stage your own base in the brown mud before Saturday; HQ24+ in the dirt is a wall the invader has to spend resources breaking.
Bank heals, teleports and speedups before the event — running out mid-fight ends your participation.

tiers.title: Core · HQ 25+ and Leadership
bullets: Hold the Capital and the Turrets. Garrison in full-health formations and cycle damaged defenders out immediately.
Lead rallies — 3–5 strong accounts, every march at full capacity. Rotate rally leads every 45–60 min so nobody fatigues.
Name a backup who is online across your window. If you are called away, they take your garrisons and the slot never goes cold.
Protect your HQ: stage it inside the mud before Saturday, shield when you sleep, and do not leave it exposed while away from the phone.
Post your availability below — leads use it to build the rotation and to close gaps before the clash starts.
